# Fixtures

Synthetic, local, replayable fixtures. **No fixture may derive from live NAS data.**

Fixtures are built at gate G3 (fixture-only implementation). This document specifies *what* must exist, so that no design decisions remain outstanding when that gate opens.

## Governing rules

1. Every fixture directory ships an `expectations` file naming the acceptance IDs it satisfies and the assertions that must hold.
2. Fixtures are produced by a committed, deterministic generator script, so repeatability is itself testable. Opaque binary blobs of unknown provenance are not acceptable fixtures.
3. Fixtures use only synthetic paths. No live share name, hostname, credential, or private filename appears in a fixture.
4. Fixtures must be non-sensitive.

## Already present

| Path | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `rules/negative/` | 47 rule sets that must fail validation, plus `expectations.yaml` naming the reason each must be rejected. Generated by `scripts/generate_negative_rule_fixtures.py`, verified by `scripts/validate_rule_config.py`. |

## Required: rule fixtures (`rules/<rule-slug>/`)

The canonical schema requires every rule to reference positive, negative, boundary, conflict, and idempotency fixtures under `tests/fixtures/rules/<slug>/`. An `active` rule requires all five to be non-empty.

## Required: identity fixtures (`identity/`)

| ID | Fixture | Expected assertions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FX-01 | Case-only collision pair | Two distinct logical files. Collision reported. Against a case-insensitive destination: mandatory review; versioning and skip strategies rejected. Never merged into one record. |
| FX-02 | NFC/NFD pair | Raw path bytes preserved verbatim; `nfc_form` correctly labelled; normalization collision reported; round-trip write and read-back populates the adapter's filename-transform capability. |
| FX-03 | Confusable pair | Confusable collision reported with both raw byte sequences displayed. |
| FX-04 | Hard-link set of three | Link count 3; one hard-link set; **not** reported as a duplicate group; links preserved where supported, blocked where not; partial retirement blocked. |
| FX-05 | Hard link versus true duplicate | Duplicate grouping contains exactly two logical members, not four. Regression test for the misgrouping defect. |
| FX-06 | Symlink, in-root relative | Not followed during enumeration or size accounting; content hash is the hash of the target **string**; recreated as a link where supported. |
| FX-07 | Symlink escaping the root | Inventoried, never followed; any operation on it fails. |
| FX-08 | Symlink, dangling | Inventoried without error; not classified unreadable; recreated as a dangling link, not resolved. |
| FX-09 | Sparse file | Apparent and allocated size both recorded and distinct; post-copy hash matches **and** the allocated-size delta is reported; a hash match alone does not set preservation-verified. |
| FX-10 | macOS package bundle | Single logical file of type `bundle`; manifest digest computed; members not independently classified or planned; partial copy fails and the partial destination is removed. |
| FX-11 | Nested bundle | Only the outermost bundle is the operable unit. |
| FX-12 | Extended-attribute bearing file | Attributes captured and compared; on an unsupporting destination the unsupported count is non-zero, the hash still matches, and the **retirement gate is not eligible** without a scoped waiver. |
| FX-13 | Resource fork and Finder info | Both captured; sidecar destinations record a declared normalization, never "preserved". |
| FX-14 | Permission and ownership variety | Mode compared; setgid stripped and reported; ownership outcome recorded, never silently skipped. |
| FX-15 | Permission-denied file | Reported, never silently skipped; content identity `unreadable`. |
| FX-16 | Concurrent modification during hashing | Change token differs across the read; hash marked unstable; bounded retry then unresolved; **the unstable hash never enters a duplicate group or a plan precondition**. |
| FX-17 | Concurrent modification during copying | Entry fails; partial destination removed or quarantined; **never reaches verified, even when the destination hash matches the precondition**. |
| FX-18 | Same-path replacement, different content | Token changed; new logical file id; old marked stale; a locked plan entry referencing the old id fails and never rebinds. |
| FX-19 | Same-path replacement, identical content | **The key test.** Token equal on size and hash but object id differs → replacement detected, review. Under an adapter without object identity the result must be indeterminate, never equal. |
| FX-20 | Coarse-timestamp same-second modification | Result is indeterminate, not equal; forces a re-hash at the precondition gate. |
| FX-21 | Truncated read / partial copy | Destination hash mismatch → entry fails; the partial destination is never promoted from its temporary name. |
| FX-22 | Corrupt transfer | Single bit flipped; hash mismatch → failure. |
| FX-23 | Zero-byte files, three of them | Identical hashes; **not** grouped as a redundancy recommendation. |
| FX-24 | Undecodable filename bytes | Encoding marked lossy; soft at inventory, blocked for operations; raw bytes preserved verbatim. |
| FX-25 | Deep path and long component | Compared against destination limits at plan time; over-limit is a plan-time block, not an execution-time surprise. |
| FX-26 | Empty directory tree | Empty directories reproduced. Regression test against naive file-only copy. |
| FX-27 | Adapter capability characterization suite | Exercises every preservation property; emits a complete capability descriptor. **This is the only valid way to produce a descriptor.** |
| FX-28 | Capability mismatch | A required property the destination cannot carry blocks entries at plan time; proceeds only with a waiver naming that property; a blanket waiver is rejected. |
| FX-29 | Descriptor drift | The descriptor in the locked plan differs from the measured one → batch stops. |
| FX-30 | Connection loss / remount | Volume identifier changes mid-run → run stops, checkpoints invalidated, in-flight tokens discarded. |

## Required: durability fixtures (`durability/`)

A fault-injecting adapter with named injection points corresponding to every step of the write protocol, so each crash-state row has its own fixture.

- Injection modes: `fail_call`, `partial_write(n)`, `succeed_then_kill`, `fsync_error_once`, `lose_unflushed_data`, `rename_indeterminate`.
- A declarable durability class per fixture volume (`strong`, `weak`, `unknown`).
- A real process-kill harness, so tests exercise actual process death rather than a simulation of it.

## Required: journal fixtures (`journal/`)

- Truncated tail at byte, mid-token, and mid-record offsets.
- Corrupt mid-file record: bit flips in the payload, in the record hash, and in the predecessor link.
- Sequence gap, sequence duplicate, chain splice, reordered records.
- Unsealed checkpoint; unsealed segment roll.
- A golden journal plus the expected canonical database dump, for the rebuild test.

## Required: approval fixtures (`approval/`)

- Matched plan and approval pairs at two versions, plus a one-byte-mutated plan.
- Consumed-approval replay; nonce replay; cross-run claim conflict.
- Expired, not-yet-valid, and clock-regressed approvals.
- Revoked before start, and revoked mid-batch.
- Rule-set changed, taxonomy changed, source drifted.
- Malicious client payloads carrying an authorization status, a validation status, an approval state, and a forged actor.
- A Sentinel-originated approval attempt.
- Scope overrun, one fixture per scope dimension.
